PyTorch does not guarantee bitwise agreement between batched, individual, CPU, or GPU computations; operation ordering and backend algorithms introduce rounding differences. TF32 can further reduce precision. Thus, packed-versus-individual discrepancies alone do not establish a padding bug. [Numerical accuracy](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html)

Recommended reference procedure: freeze identical weights and initial states, use eval mode with autocast disabled, and implement a float64 padding-skipping recurrence: update hidden states only at valid tokens, preserving them at padding. Match PyTorch’s GRU equations exactly, especially its reset gate applied after the recurrent affine transform. Compare valid-step outputs and final states against individually unpadded sequences and packed batches; compact left-padded histories into valid prefixes before packing. Read original histories at their final nonpadding position, never length−1. Vary leading padding and batch companions while preserving token order. Ordinary dense GRU processing of zero padding can change hidden states through biases and recurrence. [GRU equations](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html), [packing contract](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.utils.rnn.pack_padded_sequence.html)

Predeclare tolerances and fixtures before evaluating the implementation. PyTorch’s documented assert_close defaults provide starting thresholds: float32 rtol=1.3e−6, atol=1e−5; float64 both 1e−7, using |actual−reference|≤atol+rtol·|reference|. These are general defaults, not GRU error guarantees. Report maximum absolute error and failing-element counts. On failure, retain thresholds and repeat with TF32 explicitly disabled, cuDNN disabled, and CPU float64. Padding-dependent discrepancies persisting against the float64 reference indicate semantic problems; discrepancies shrinking with higher precision support a numerical explanation without proving correctness. [Tolerance documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/testing), [backend precision controls](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/cuda)
